record.paper_title: Enabling and Emerging Technologies for Social Distancing: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Bluetooth privacy adoption and localization robustness
record.original_question: How can Bluetooth-based social distancing systems for contact tracing, crowd detection, and estimating the distance between two people protect user privacy, encourage users to share the necessary information, remain accurate when phones or wearable devices are inside pockets or bags, operate despite the need for Bluetooth to stay enabled, and combine with technologies such as Wi-Fi to improve localization accuracy?

evidence.quote: However, the privacy of users needs to be taken into account as the applications require users to share information with the authorities and third parties. This can be a research direction to ensure privacy and encourage people to share their information to prevent the spreading of diseases.

In addition, several drawbacks of Bluetooth technology in social distancing which need to be considered such as the accuracy of localization techniques when the users’ devices are located inside the pockets or bags and their devices always need to turn on the Bluetooth mode. Furthermore, combining Bluetooth and other technologies (e.g., Wi-Fi [77]) to improve the localization accuracy is also an open research direction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a system for social distancing that uses Bluetooth-enabled smartphones and/or wearable devices carried by individuals in a population. The system is required to perform three tasks: (i) contact tracing, i.e. recording, for each user, the set of other users with whom that user has been in close proximity over a recent time window; (ii) crowd detection, i.e. estimating the number and density of people in a given region; and (iii) pairwise distance estimation between two devices using Bluetooth signal measurements (e.g., RSSI), possibly fused with other radio technologies such as Wi-Fi.

Design a protocol and accompanying signal-processing/estimation methodology that simultaneously satisfies the following requirements:

1. Privacy: Provide a formal privacy guarantee (for example, in the sense of differential privacy, cryptographic indistinguishability, or a comparable model) for the data shared by users with health authorities or third parties, so that an adversary observing the messages exchanged and the data uploaded cannot link contact events or location traces to specific identifiable users beyond a quantified bound.

2. Incentive compatibility: Provide a mechanism (e.g., a reward scheme, mechanism-design protocol, or game-theoretic argument) under which it is in each user's interest to truthfully share the information required by the system, so that participation and disclosure form an equilibrium.

3. Robustness of localization: Achieve pairwise distance estimates whose mean-squared error remains bounded by a prescribed tolerance even when the transmitting and/or receiving device is occluded, e.g., placed inside a pocket or a bag, which produces non-line-of-sight attenuation and orientation-dependent fading of the Bluetooth signal.

4. Energy and availability constraints: Operate under the constraint that Bluetooth radios must remain enabled on user devices, and quantify (and minimize) the resulting energy consumption and availability impact.

5. Multi-modal fusion: Specify how Bluetooth measurements may be combined with Wi-Fi (and possibly other) measurements in an estimator whose localization accuracy provably improves over the Bluetooth-only estimator under a stated channel model.

Either construct such a protocol together with rigorous proofs of the above properties, or prove an impossibility result showing that the five requirements cannot be jointly satisfied within a specified model.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a multi-part open research direction in privacy-preserving contact tracing and indoor localization. While many partial advances exist (e.g., DP-3T and Google/Apple Exposure Notifications for privacy, BLE+Wi-Fi fusion methods for localization), no single solution simultaneously satisfies all five requirements with formal guarantees. The problem remains open as a joint research challenge.

status_evidence.title: Decentralized Privacy-Preserving Proximity Tracing (DP-3T)
status_evidence.snippet: Protocol providing privacy guarantees for Bluetooth proximity tracing, but does not address pocket/bag occlusion or multi-modal fusion.
status_evidence.claim: Privacy aspect partially addressed; localization robustness and incentive compatibility not jointly handled.

status_evidence.title: Surveys on BLE-based indoor localization
status_evidence.snippet: Combining Bluetooth and other technologies (e.g., Wi-Fi) to improve the localization accuracy is also an open research direction.
status_evidence.claim: The combined problem is identified as open.
